scope: Node CPU mechanics only: actual preparePack, GLTFLoader/createSuite, quaternion and morph writes, Object3D matrix updates, canonical events, and CPU resource ownership. No WebGLRenderer or browser run.
exclusions: No GPU draw, skinning shader, GPU memory, browser input, frame rate, or hardware device claim.
Morph/skin vertex counts govern preflight/loading and hypothetical GPU deformation; advance writes channels and matrices, not all vertices.
Heap snapshots are process-wide observations with uncontrolled GC; they prove neither leak freedom nor zero allocation.
Shared cloud CPU scheduling, JIT and GC are uncontrolled; repeated within-process runs are observations, not independent machine trials.

preparePack.description: Filesystem reader + JSON validation + SHA-256 integrity + numeric GLB preflight. Files were just generated; this is not cold-disk I/O.

preflightOnly.description: preflightGLB on already resident bytes; includes bounded float/index/skin scans.

create.decodedCache: empty initially; actor 1 decodes, later actors reuse decoded source

steady.description: Timed loop calls suite.advance for every actor at each distinct animation time. Playback enqueue/start is outside each batch timer. Percentiles are over batch means, not individual call latency.

individual.description: One timing bracket around one group advance, including its actor loop. Includes timer overhead; not renderer or end-to-end frame latency.

queue.description: Enqueue timer includes validation, event allocation and sorting. Processing timer excludes enqueue and includes all due events plus the final sample/matrix update. Event means are throughput, not per-event latency.

mixed.description: Timed advance loop with play enqueue and event processing every 60 group ticks (synthetic 240 Hz canonical time). Batch-throughput metric.

idle.description: Explicit idle advance calls; the demand scheduler would ordinarily avoid these calls. This is not a zero-work idle renderer result.

actorPool.description: Concurrent ActorPool.create invokes actual createSuite/GLTFLoader. Limits are explicitly sized to this actor group, which can exceed default limits. Source bytes reserve one unique encoded GLB, not decoded heap, GPU memory, or caller-owned prepared bytes.
